newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up on strong Northwest physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up on strong Northwest physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Friday, led by higher physical power prices in the California Oregon Border (COB) market, industry sources said.

"COB is actually leading this market -- when you look at $20 (per megawatt hour) trading in the next-day (COB) market then you look at May (futures) at $14, you have a lot of room for upward movement," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1230 EDT, May COB was trading up 81 cents at $14.10 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchange in a range of $13.75-14.20, while June COB was up 62 cents at $13.50 after trade in a range of $13.35-13.65 per MWh.
October COB was up 35 cents at $18.50 per MWh.
May Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 80 cents at $17.75 after reaching as low as $17.40, while June was up 40 cents at $18.60 after trade in a range of $18.40-18.65 per MWh.
September PV had traded up five cents at $23.25 per MWh.
Sources said the real-time power market was strong, especially in the Northwest, with Bonneville Power Authority (BPA) not offering any surplus power and reported to be purchasing some electricity.

Northwest generation will also be impacted by a planned outage at the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 on the central California coast, set to shut Saturday for a 36-day refueling and maintenance outage, the sources said.
Also, water reservoir levels were reported to be relatively low in the Northwest, although those levels were expected to rise as a late spring water runoff begins in earnest.
Hydroelectric generation was expected to be strong, but was being delayed by the late runoff, trigged by cool Northwest weather, the sources said.
Palo Verde futures continued to see some strength from expectations of above-normal weather over the short term, the sources said.

Forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to be four to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal into the middle of next week, while temperatures in the Northwest were called to average two to six degrees above normal through the weekend.
NYMEX said that as of 1210 EDT an estimated total of 413 COB and 131 PV contracts had traded.
In Western generation, the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit remained shut for refueling and maintenance, with an expected restart date in late June.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was also shut for refueling, and was expected to resume power output in early July.
In addition, nearly 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was off-line in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance, as well as hydropower displacement sales.
COB open interest for April 17 rose 141 to 4,300, while PV open interest rose 499 to 5,285, NYMEX said.
